thesis: We stay where it hurts because leaving feels more frightening than suffering, and every year we give makes the next year harder to refuse.

chain: Each year he stays, the cost of leaving looks bigger (the years would be 'wasted').
So he stays another year, which adds to the pile.
The pile is the past; it does not change what the next year is worth.

premise: The years he has given are physically in his office: one binder per year on his desk, 2019 to 2024, and old boxes on the floor. The door has been there the whole time.

motif.object: the binder stack and the door

moments.understand: The day is over and he is still here, waiting.
Six years are stacked on his desk; he knows he hates it.
The life he wants is literally outside the window.
He goes back; the light goes out of the day.
The door is right there; leaving is what scares him.
Another year lands on the stack: the more he gives, the harder he holds on.
The question is the next year, not the past ones: he walks to the open door.

rejected: a cage (a ready-made metaphor that replaces the place with a symbol)
a scale with years (an infographic that interrupts the story)
